gallery.title: File:120810-N-GL340-069 (7775523438).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: From left to right, Cambodian Major General Pen Ra, U.S. Navy Capt. Jim Morgan, Sihanouk province Deputy Governor Prack Chansokha and U.S. Navy Rear Adm. Kate Gregory cut a ribbon during a ribbon cutting ceremony at The O Chrov Health Center in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, Aug. 10, 2012, as part of Pacific Partnership 2012 (PP12). Pacific Partnership is an annual deployment of forces designed to strengthen maritime and humanitarian partnerships during disaster relief operations, while providing humanitarian, medical, dental and engineering assistance to nations of the Pacific. (DoD photo by Mass Communication Specialist 3rd Class Michael Feddersen, U.S. Navy/Released)
categories: Photographs by the United States Department of Defense with bad file names

gallery.title: File:120803-O-ZZ999-024 (7726653048).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: U.S. Navy Lt. Christopher Chung watches as Kong Bunho, a member of the Royal Cambodian Air Force, performs a dental procedure during a medical civic action project (MEDCAP) at Kandol Dom Primary School for Pacific Partnership 2012 in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, Aug. 3, 2012. MEDCAPs provide free medical, dental and optometry care to host nation patients and provide training and subject matter exchanges between the service members and civilians working on PP12 and the host nation medical personnel. Pacific Partnership is an annual deployment of forces designed to strengthen maritime and humanitarian partnerships during disaster relief operations, while providing humanitarian, medical, dental and engineering assistance to nations of the Pacific. (DoD photo by Kristopher Radder, U.S. Navy/Released)

gallery.description: U.S. Marine Corps Maj. Brett Ellis, above, with the Marine Medium Helicopter Squadron (HMM) 268 Reinforced, embarked aboard the amphibious transport dock ship USS New Orleans (LPD-18), plays with a Cambodian child during a community outreach project at the School of Public Health and Social Work of St. Elizabeth in Cambodia Dec. 19, 2011. The New Orleans and embarked Marines assigned to the 11th Marine Expeditionary Unit were operating in the U.S. 7th Fleet area of responsibility as part of the Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group.
